stem: A project costs Rs 1,00,000 today. It returns Rs 60,500 at end of year 1 and Rs 66,550 at end of year 2. The discount rate is 10% per annum. What is the NPV? [Use: 1/1.1 = 0.9091; 1/(1.1)² = 0.8264]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student adds undiscounted cash flows and subtracts cost: (60,500 + 66,550) - 1,00,000 = 27,050, ignoring discounting.
Student discounts only year 1 and takes year 2 at face value: 55,000 + 66,550 - 1,00,000 = 21,550.
Student uses 5% (half the stated rate) as the discount rate, computing inflated present values and a higher NPV of Rs 17,982.

explanation: NPV = sum of present values of cash flows minus the initial cost. PV1 = 60,500 / 1.1 = 55,000. PV2 = 66,550 / (1.1)² = 66,550 / 1.21 = 55,000. NPV = 55,000 + 55,000 - 1,00,000 = Rs 10,000.
